package_info.why_malicious: This document does not describe a specific malicious package, but rather discusses best practices for detecting malicious code in software supply chains, such as binary analysis and reproducible builds. No individual package or code is identified as malicious in this report.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected or undocumented functionality in final binaries
Presence of secrets or credentials embedded in production binaries
Discrepancies between source code and built binary (non-reproducible builds)
Inclusion of Software of Unknown Provenance (SOUP) in deliverables
file_indicators: Binaries with undocumented dependencies or modules
Build artifacts that differ from reproducible builds
network_indicators: N/A (no specific network indicators described in this report)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Use binary analysis tools to inspect final software packages for hidden functionality, embedded secrets, or undocumented dependencies. Validate that builds are reproducible to ensure no tampering or unauthorized modifications have occurred. Compare SBOMs generated from source code and binary analysis to identify transitive or hidden dependencies. Apply these practices both to internally developed and third-party commercial software before deployment.
